tagline: Eighteen miles, timed by the buffalo.
intro: From the Blue Bell entrance on the west side of Custer State Park, the Wildlife Loop bends in a long U for 18 miles to the east entrance, twisting through prairie and ponderosa hills. The park puts the drive at an hour and a half and adds that the time depends on wildlife jams.

The park calls the buffalo its number one inhabitant. The herd began with thirty-six animals bought in 1914, and each fall riders gather it in a roundup held officially since 1965. In December 2017 the Legion Lake Fire jumped the road and in one night grew from 6 square miles to 55, burning most of the country around it.

moments.title: Blue Bell
moments.text: Named for the native bluebells, the place had a post office only from 1932 to 1941, though its public lodge goes back to 1925.

moments.title: The burros
moments.text: Near the southeastern tip of the loop a band of burros descended from the miners' pack animals begs at passing cars, though park rules forbid feeding any wildlife.

practical: The road is open year-round with a South Dakota state park entrance license, and it calls for careful driving in winter conditions.
